title: 1989 AHSME Problem 24
statement: Five people are sitting at a round table. Let \(f\ge0\) be the number of people sitting next to at least one female and \(m\ge0\) be the number of people sitting next to at least one male. The number of possible ordered pairs \((f,m)\) is

solutions.text:
For \(0,1,2\) females, the possible pairs are respectively \[ \begin{aligned} &(0,5),\ (2,5),\\ &(4,5),\ (3,4), \end{aligned} \] where the two-female cases distinguish adjacent from nonadjacent females. Swapping the sexes gives \[ \begin{aligned} &(5,0),\ (5,2),\\ &(5,4),\ (4,3). \end{aligned} \] These are \(8\) distinct ordered pairs.

Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: Classify arrangements by the number of females
With two females, separate the adjacent and nonadjacent cases; obtain three-female cases by symmetry
